"""Deterministic Raft leader-election and log-replication simulation.

The simulation advances virtual time only: it never reads the wall clock and
never uses randomness, so identical input produces byte-identical output.

The core execution path is split by responsibility: scenario normalization
(:mod:`.scenario`), the deterministic event queue (:mod:`.events`), network
delivery and fault determination (:mod:`.network`), node state transitions
(:mod:`.protocol`) and final report generation (:mod:`.report`). The
``simulate``, ``explore`` and ``replay`` entry points all run through the
single :class:`_Simulator` core below.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from .events import (
    _KIND_CLIENT,
    _KIND_FAULT,
    _KIND_HEARTBEAT,
    _KIND_LIVENESS,
    _KIND_MEMBERSHIP,
    _KIND_MESSAGE,
    _KIND_NODE_EVENT,
    _KIND_REACTION,
    _KIND_READ,
    _KIND_TIMEOUT,
    EventQueue,
)
from .network import Network
from .node import (
    CONFIG_JOINT,
    CONFIG_STABLE,
    KIND_COMMAND,
    KIND_CONFIG,
    ROLE_CANDIDATE,
    ROLE_FOLLOWER,
    ROLE_LEADER,
    ROLE_PRECANDIDATE,
    _Node,
)
from .protocol import _Protocol
from .report import build_report
from .scenario import ScenarioError, _is_int, _require_int, parse_scenario


class _Simulator(_Protocol):
    """The single core execution path: wires the event queue, the network
    layer and the protocol transitions together and advances virtual time."""

    def __init__(self, config: dict) -> None:
        self.node_names: list[str] = config["nodes"]
        self.duration: int = config["duration"]
        self.timeouts: dict[str, int] = config["electionTimeouts"]
        self.heartbeat_interval: int = config["heartbeatInterval"]
        self.faults: list[dict] = config["faults"]
        self.commands: list[dict] = config["clientCommands"]
        self.node_events: list[dict] = config["nodeEvents"]
        self.node_events_provided: bool = config["nodeEventsProvided"]
        self.pre_vote_enabled: bool = config["preVote"]
        self.snapshot_threshold: int | None = config["snapshotThreshold"]
        self.membership_enabled: bool = config["membershipEnabled"]
        self.changes: list[dict] = config["membershipChanges"] or []
        if self.membership_enabled:
            initial_members = frozenset(config["initialMembers"])
            self.initial_config: dict = {
                "type": CONFIG_STABLE,
                "old": initial_members,
                "new": initial_members,
            }
        else:
            all_nodes = frozenset(self.node_names)
            self.initial_config = {"type": CONFIG_STABLE, "old": all_nodes, "new": all_nodes}
        self.state = {name: _Node() for name in self.node_names}
        self.index = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(self.node_names)}
        self.timeline: list[dict] = []
        self.leaders_by_term: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
        # The deterministic event queue and the network layer (delay model,
        # partitions, per-message faults) form the transport; the clock and
        # drain phase stay on the simulator and are read through callbacks.
        self.queue = EventQueue()
        self.now = 0
        # While draining client commands (and the replication cascade they
        # trigger), new messages land in the REACTION phase instead of the
        # regular MESSAGE phase.
        self.reaction_phase = False
        self.network = Network(
            config["messageDelay"],
            config["messageFaults"],
            self.queue,
            self._record,
            lambda: self.now,
            lambda: self.reaction_phase,
        )
        # Commands rejected at the door (target was not leader, or was down)
        # never reach a log. Final committed / superseded / pending outcomes
        # are derived from the end state; reason and knownLeader are captured
        # at rejection time.
        self.rejected: dict[str, dict] = {}
        # Membership-change bookkeeping.
        # change_id -> {"node", "action", "member", "result", "index"?, "term"?,
        #               "jointIndex"?, "stableIndex"?, "reason"?}
        self.change_results: dict[str, dict] = {}
        # change_id of the change whose joint entry is committed but whose
        # stable entry has not been appended yet, if any.
        # Learner catch-up state for the in-progress add: once the target
        # learner's matchIndex reaches the pre-joint log end, the leader
        # appends the joint config entry.
        self.pending_catchup: dict | None = None
        # Read-only query bookkeeping.
        self.read_queries: list[dict] = config["readQueries"]
        self.read_queries_provided: bool = config["readQueriesProvided"]
        # query id -> {"node", "term", "readIndex", "config", "acks",
        #              "required"} for accepted queries still awaiting a
        # same-term majority confirmation under the recorded configuration.
        self.pending_reads: dict[str, dict] = {}
        # query id -> final outcome for queries resolved during the run.
        self.read_results: dict[str, dict] = {}
        # query id -> client-command ids already committed when the query was
        # accepted; a completed read omitting any of them is a stale read.
        self.read_required: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
        # Client-command ids committed so far (leader-side commit advances).
        self.committed_command_ids: set[str] = set()
        # Client-command ids accepted (appended to a leader's log) at least
        # once; together with the rejected map and current log presence this
        # distinguishes "not submitted yet / pending" from "superseded".
        self.accepted_command_ids: set[str] = set()
        # Optional liveness checks. Each one is evaluated at every virtual
        # timestamp in its [startTime, deadline] window, but only after all
        # pre-existing events sharing that timestamp (and their zero-delay
        # reaction cascades) have drained; checks at the same timestamp run in
        # input order.
        self.liveness_checks: list[dict] = config["livenessChecks"]
        self.liveness_provided: bool = config["livenessChecksProvided"]
        # check id -> finished result entry (status satisfied/failed).
        self.liveness_results: dict[str, dict] = {}
        # Whether an online leader exists at the current evaluation point.
        self.leader_online = False
        # change id -> virtual time its stable configuration entry was first
        # applied on any node (the moment the change is committed).
        self.stable_commit_times: dict[str, int] = {}

    def run(self) -> dict:
        for order, fault in enumerate(self.faults):
            self.queue.push((fault["time"], _KIND_FAULT, order, fault))
        for order, event in enumerate(self.node_events):
            self.queue.push((event["time"], _KIND_NODE_EVENT, order, event))
        for order, command in enumerate(self.commands):
            self.queue.push((command["time"], _KIND_CLIENT, order, command))
        for order, change in enumerate(self.changes):
            self.queue.push((change["time"], _KIND_MEMBERSHIP, order, change))
        for order, query in enumerate(self.read_queries):
            self.queue.push((query["time"], _KIND_READ, order, query))
        for name in self.node_names:
            if self._is_voter(name, self.initial_config):
                self.queue.push((self.timeouts[name], _KIND_TIMEOUT, self.index[name], (name, 0)))
        if self.liveness_provided:
            # Anchors at every window edge guarantee evaluation also runs at
            # timestamps carrying no pre-existing events; all other timestamps
            # are reached via the drain hook in the loop below.
            anchors = sorted({
                edge
                for check in self.liveness_checks
                for edge in (check["startTime"], check["deadline"])
            })
            for order, edge in enumerate(anchors):
                self.queue.push((edge, _KIND_LIVENESS, order, None))
        while self.queue:
            time, kind, _order, payload = self.queue.pop()
            if time > self.duration:
                break
            self.now = time
            self.reaction_phase = kind in (_KIND_CLIENT, _KIND_MEMBERSHIP, _KIND_READ, _KIND_REACTION)
            if kind == _KIND_FAULT:
                self.network.apply_fault(payload)
            elif kind == _KIND_NODE_EVENT:
                self._on_node_event(payload)
            elif kind in (_KIND_MESSAGE, _KIND_REACTION):
                self._deliver(payload)
            elif kind == _KIND_CLIENT:
                self._on_client_command(payload)
            elif kind == _KIND_MEMBERSHIP:
                self._on_membership_change(payload)
            elif kind == _KIND_READ:
                self._on_read_query(payload)
            elif kind == _KIND_TIMEOUT:
                self._on_timeout(*payload)
            elif kind == _KIND_HEARTBEAT:
                self._on_heartbeat(*payload)
            # The liveness anchor itself is a no-op: it only marks a window
            # edge that carries no other events. Either way, once no entry
            # remains for the current timestamp (its zero-delay reactions
            # included), the timestamp has fully drained and the checks run.
            if (
                self.liveness_provided
                and self.liveness_checks
                and (not self.queue or self.queue.next_time > self.now)
            ):
                self._evaluate_liveness(self.now)
        return build_report(self)


def run_simulation(raw: object) -> dict:
    """Validate a decoded JSON scenario and run the deterministic simulation."""
    return _Simulator(parse_scenario(raw)).run()

"""Per-node persistent and volatile state.

``_Node`` holds one server's full state — persisted fields (term, vote, log,
snapshot, commit/apply progress) and volatile ones (role, replication
progress, pre-vote round, leader-contact clock) — together with the log and
configuration views over them. It contains no simulation logic of its own.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

ROLE_FOLLOWER = "follower"
ROLE_CANDIDATE = "candidate"
ROLE_LEADER = "leader"
# Optional pre-vote phase: a preCandidate probes the cluster with a
# prospective term (current term + 1) without touching its persisted term or
# votedFor, so a node rejoining after an isolation gap cannot disrupt a
# stable leader with a meaningless high term.
ROLE_PRECANDIDATE = "preCandidate"

# Log-entry kinds: ordinary client commands versus replicated configuration
# entries created by joint-consensus membership changes.
KIND_COMMAND = "command"
KIND_CONFIG = "config"
CONFIG_JOINT = "joint"
CONFIG_STABLE = "stable"


class _Node:
    __slots__ = (
        "role",
        "term",
        "voted_for",
        "known_leader",
        "votes",
        "timeout_gen",
        "log",
        "snapshot_index",
        "snapshot_term",
        "snapshot_config",
        "commit_index",
        "last_applied",
        "applied",
        "next_index",
        "match_index",
        "online",
        "restart_count",
        "pre_round",
        "pre_term",
        "pre_votes",
        "pre_config",
        "leader_contact",
    )

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.role = ROLE_FOLLOWER
        self.term = 0
        self.voted_for: str | None = None
        self.known_leader: str | None = None
        self.votes: set[str] = set()
        self.timeout_gen = 0
        # Log entries keep their global indices: self.log holds only the
        # uncompacted suffix, so entry for global index i is self.log[i - 1 -
        # self.snapshot_index]. snapshot_index/snapshot_term describe the last
        # entry folded into the (modeled) snapshot; 0 means no snapshot yet.
        self.log: list[dict] = []
        self.snapshot_index = 0
        self.snapshot_term = 0
        # Configuration in effect at snapshot_index (None before any
        # snapshot). Config entries can be compacted into snapshots like any
        # committed entry, so membership survives compaction.
        self.snapshot_config: dict | None = None
        self.commit_index = 0
        self.last_applied = 0
        self.applied: list[dict] = []
        # Leader-only replication progress, keyed by peer name.
        self.next_index: dict[str, int] = {}
        self.match_index: dict[str, int] = {}
        # Crash/restart lifecycle. term, voted_for, log, snapshot_index,
        # snapshot_term, snapshot_config, commit_index, last_applied, applied
        # and the configuration encoded in the log all model persisted state:
        # every change to them is made (synchronously) before the response that
        # depends on it, so they survive a crash and are simply kept on
        # restart. Everything else is volatile and is reset on restart.
        self.online = True
        self.restart_count = 0
        # Optional pre-vote phase state (volatile; never persisted). A
        # preCandidate probes with prospective term pre_term = term + 1 and
        # round pre_round without changing term or voted_for; pre_votes holds
        # the peers that granted the active round and pre_config the electorate
        # that round is decided under. All four are reset on restart.
        self.pre_round = 0
        self.pre_term = 0
        self.pre_votes: set[str] = set()
        self.pre_config: dict | None = None
        # Virtual time of the most recent heartbeat/appendEntries/
        # installSnapshot accepted from a current-term leader, or -1 when no
        # such contact has occurred since the term began (or since startup or
        # restart). A pre-vote is granted only when no contact is recorded or
        # the local election timeout has elapsed since the latest contact.
        # Purely internal: it is never serialized.
        self.leader_contact = -1

    def last_log_index(self) -> int:
        return self.snapshot_index + len(self.log)

    def last_log_term(self) -> int:
        return self.log[-1]["term"] if self.log else self.snapshot_term

    def term_at(self, index: int) -> int:
        if index <= 0:
            return 0
        if index == self.snapshot_index:
            return self.snapshot_term
        if index < self.snapshot_index:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} is covered by the snapshot")
        return self.log[index - 1 - self.snapshot_index]["term"]

    def has_entry(self, index: int) -> bool:
        return self.snapshot_index < index <= self.last_log_index()

    def config_at(self, index: int, initial_config: dict) -> dict | None:
        """The configuration in effect immediately *before* the entry at
        ``index`` is applied: the latest config entry with a smaller index, or
        the snapshot config / initial configuration. Returns None when no
        configuration entry precedes ``index`` (the caller substitutes the
        initial configuration)."""
        config = self.snapshot_config if self.snapshot_config else initial_config
        upper = min(index - 1, self.last_log_index())
        for i in range(self.snapshot_index + 1, upper + 1):
            entry = self.log[i - 1 - self.snapshot_index]
            if entry.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG:
                config = entry["config"]
        return config

    def latest_config(self, initial_config: dict) -> dict:
        """The newest configuration present in this node's log (or its
        snapshot), whether or not it is committed or applied."""
        result = self.snapshot_config if self.snapshot_config else initial_config
        for entry in self.log:
            if entry.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG:
                result = entry["config"]
        return result

    def committed_config(self, initial_config: dict) -> dict:
        """The configuration established by the newest committed config
        entry (or the snapshot config, which only covers committed state)."""
        config = self.snapshot_config if self.snapshot_config else initial_config
        upper = min(self.commit_index, self.last_log_index())
        for i in range(self.snapshot_index + 1, upper + 1):
            entry = self.log[i - 1 - self.snapshot_index]
            if entry.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG:
                config = entry["config"]
        return config

12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	from .events import _KIND_MESSAGE, _KIND_REACTION, EventQueue
15

18	    """Read-confirmation messages (readProbe/readReply) carry the query id
19	    into their timeline entries; no other message kind has one."""

35

37	    entry, and ``clock`` / ``in_reaction_phase`` read the core loop's current
38	    virtual time and drain phase so zero-delay reactions are scheduled into
39	    the right event kind.
40	    """
41	
42	    def __init__(
43	        self,
44	        delay: int,
45	        message_fault_rules: list[dict],
46	        queue: EventQueue,
47	        record,
48	        clock,
49	        in_reaction_phase,
50	    ) -> None:
51	        self.delay = delay
52	        # Per-message fault rules, keyed by the full selector
53	        # (from, to, message, occurrence); the per-(from, to, message) send
54	        # counter below numbers actual sends from the start of the run.
55	        self.message_faults: dict[tuple, dict] = {
56	            (rule["from"], rule["to"], rule["message"], rule["occurrence"]): rule
57	            for rule in message_fault_rules
58	        }
59	        self.message_fault_counts: dict[tuple, int] = {}
60	        self.partition: list[frozenset[str]] | None = None
61	        self.send_counter = 0
62	        self.queue = queue
63	        self.record = record
64	        self._clock = clock
65	        self._in_reaction_phase = in_reaction_phase
66	
67	    def apply_fault(self, fault: dict) -> None:
68	        if fault["action"] == "partition":
69	            self.partition = [frozenset(group) for group in fault["groups"]]
70	            self.record({"type": "fault", "action": "partition", "groups": fault["groups"]})
71	        else:
72	            self.partition = None
73	            self.record({"type": "fault", "action": "heal"})
74	
75	    def connected(self, a: str, b: str) -> bool:
76	        if self.partition is None:
77	            return True
78	        return any(a in group and b in group for group in self.partition)
79	
80	    def send(self, src: str, dst: str, msg: dict) -> None:
81	        self.record({
82	            "type": "messageSend",
83	            "node": src,
84	            "peer": dst,
85	            "message": msg["kind"],
86	            "term": msg["term"],
87	            **_query_id_field(msg),
88	            **_pre_vote_fields(msg),
89	        })
90	        self.send_counter += 1
91	        envelope = {**msg, "src": src, "dst": dst}
92	        # A messageFaults rule matches the occurrence-th actual send of its
93	        # (from, to, message) selector. The fault is recorded right after the
94	        # send; a drop replaces delivery with a dropped/messageFault result at
95	        # the originally scheduled arrival, a delay shifts the arrival itself.
96	        count_key = (src, dst, msg["kind"])
97	        occurrence = self.message_fault_counts.get(count_key, 0) + 1
98	        self.message_fault_counts[count_key] = occurrence
99	        rule = self.message_faults.get((src, dst, msg["kind"], occurrence))
100	        extra_delay = 0
101	        if rule is not None:
102	            scheduled = self._clock() + self.delay
103	            fault_entry = {
104	                "type": "messageFault",
105	                "rule": rule["index"],
106	                "from": src,
107	                "to": dst,
108	                "message": msg["kind"],
109	                "occurrence": occurrence,
110	                "action": rule["action"],
111	                "scheduledTime": scheduled,
112	            }

115	            else:

121	        # batch shares the batch's timestamp and must follow the remaining
122	        # client commands; a positive delay lands strictly in the future and
123	        # queues as a normal message arrival.
124	        in_phase = self._in_reaction_phase() and effective_delay == 0
125	        kind = _KIND_REACTION if in_phase else _KIND_MESSAGE

129	        """Decide the fate of an arriving envelope. A drop (messageFault
130	        rule, destination down, partition) is recorded here and reported as
131	        False; True means the message must be dispatched to its handler."""
132	        src, dst = msg["src"], msg["dst"]

135	            # receiver, reported at its originally scheduled arrival time.
136	            self.record({
137	                "type": "messageResult",
138	                "node": dst,
139	                "peer": src,
140	                "message": msg["kind"],
141	                "term": msg["term"],
142	                **_query_id_field(msg),
143	                **_pre_vote_fields(msg),

145	                "reason": "messageFault",
146	            })
147	            return False
148	        if not dst_online:
149	            # The destination crashed after this message was sent; it is
150	            # dropped on arrival. Messages the crashed node itself sent
151	            # earlier are unaffected and still land at their original time.
152	            self.record({
153	                "type": "messageResult",
154	                "node": dst,
155	                "peer": src,
156	                "message": msg["kind"],
157	                "term": msg["term"],
158	                **_query_id_field(msg),
159	                **_pre_vote_fields(msg),
160	                "result": "dropped",
161	                "reason": "nodeDown",
162	            })

169	                "message": msg["kind"],

        self.queue = queue
        self.record = record
        self._clock = clock
        self._in_reaction_phase = in_reaction_phase

    def apply_fault(self, fault: dict) -> None:
        if fault["action"] == "partition":
            self.partition = [frozenset(group) for group in fault["groups"]]
            self.record({"type": "fault", "action": "partition", "groups": fault["groups"]})
        else:
            self.partition = None
            self.record({"type": "fault", "action": "heal"})

    def connected(self, a: str, b: str) -> bool:
        if self.partition is None:
            return True
        return any(a in group and b in group for group in self.partition)

    def send(self, src: str, dst: str, msg: dict) -> None:
        self.record({
            "type": "messageSend",
            "node": src,
            "peer": dst,
            "message": msg["kind"],
            "term": msg["term"],
            **_query_id_field(msg),
            **_pre_vote_fields(msg),
        })
        self.send_counter += 1
        envelope = {**msg, "src": src, "dst": dst}
        # A messageFaults rule matches the occurrence-th actual send of its
        # (from, to, message) selector. The fault is recorded right after the
        # send; a drop replaces delivery with a dropped/messageFault result at
        # the originally scheduled arrival, a delay shifts the arrival itself.
        count_key = (src, dst, msg["kind"])
        occurrence = self.message_fault_counts.get(count_key, 0) + 1
        self.message_fault_counts[count_key] = occurrence
        rule = self.message_faults.get((src, dst, msg["kind"], occurrence))
        extra_delay = 0
        if rule is not None:
            scheduled = self._clock() + self.delay
            fault_entry = {
                "type": "messageFault",
                "rule": rule["index"],
                "from": src,
                "to": dst,
                "message": msg["kind"],
                "occurrence": occurrence,
                "action": rule["action"],
                "scheduledTime": scheduled,
            }
            if rule["action"] == "drop":
                envelope["faultDrop"] = True
            else:
                extra_delay = rule["delay"]
                fault_entry["arrivalTime"] = scheduled + extra_delay
            self.record(fault_entry)
        effective_delay = self.delay + extra_delay
        # Zero-delay replication triggered while draining a client-command
        # batch shares the batch's timestamp and must follow the remaining
        # client commands; a positive delay lands strictly in the future and
        # queues as a normal message arrival.
        in_phase = self._in_reaction_phase() and effective_delay == 0
        kind = _KIND_REACTION if in_phase else _KIND_MESSAGE
        self.queue.push((self._clock() + effective_delay, kind, self.send_counter, envelope))

    def deliver(self, msg: dict, dst_online: bool) -> bool:
        """Decide the fate of an arriving envelope. A drop (messageFault
        rule, destination down, partition) is recorded here and reported as
        False; True means the message must be dispatched to its handler."""
        src, dst = msg["src"], msg["dst"]
        if msg.get("faultDrop"):
            # A messageFaults drop rule: the message never reaches the
            # receiver, reported at its originally scheduled arrival time.
            self.record({
                "type": "messageResult",
                "node": dst,
                "peer": src,
                "message": msg["kind"],
                "term": msg["term"],
                **_query_id_field(msg),
                **_pre_vote_fields(msg),
                "result": "dropped",
                "reason": "messageFault",
            })
            return False
        if not dst_online:
            # The destination crashed after this message was sent; it is
            # dropped on arrival. Messages the crashed node itself sent
            # earlier are unaffected and still land at their original time.
            self.record({
                "type": "messageResult",
                "node": dst,
                "peer": src,
                "message": msg["kind"],
                "term": msg["term"],
                **_query_id_field(msg),
                **_pre_vote_fields(msg),
                "result": "dropped",
                "reason": "nodeDown",
            })
            return False
        if not self.connected(src, dst):
            self.record({
                "type": "messageResult",
                "node": dst,
                "peer": src,
                "message": msg["kind"],
                "term": msg["term"],
                **_query_id_field(msg),
                **_pre_vote_fields(msg),
                "result": "dropped",
                "reason": "partition",
            })
            return False
        return True

"""Deterministic virtual-time event queue.

Events are ordered by (virtual time, kind, scheduling order): all events
sharing a timestamp drain in kind order, and same-kind events drain in the
order they were scheduled. The queue only ever holds virtual timestamps; it
never reads the wall clock.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import heapq

# Event kinds, processed in this order when they share a timestamp.
_KIND_FAULT = 0
_KIND_NODE_EVENT = 1
_KIND_MESSAGE = 2
_KIND_CLIENT = 3
# Replication traffic triggered by client commands (and its replies) lands
# here so that, even with zero message delay, all client commands sharing a
# timestamp are handled in input order before their reactions drain.
_KIND_REACTION = 4
# Membership requests sit behind every pending reaction: the heap keeps
# (t, REACTION, ...) entries ahead of (t, MEMBERSHIP, ...), so a request's own
# zero-delay cascade likewise drains before the next timed event.
_KIND_MEMBERSHIP = 5
# Read-only queries are accepted after faults, node events, arrived messages,
# client commands (and their zero-delay reactions) and membership requests,
# and before timeouts and heartbeats; a query's own zero-delay probe cascade
# likewise drains before the next timed event.
_KIND_READ = 6
_KIND_TIMEOUT = 7
_KIND_HEARTBEAT = 8
# Liveness checks are evaluated after every pre-existing event (and its
# zero-delay reaction cascade) sharing the timestamp has drained, so this is
# the largest event kind.
_KIND_LIVENESS = 9


class EventQueue:
    """A deterministic priority queue of ``(time, kind, order, payload)``
    events. ``order`` is a monotonically assigned sequence number per
    scheduling site, so events comparing equal on ``(time, kind)`` drain in
    scheduling order and the payload never takes part in comparisons."""

    __slots__ = ("_heap",)

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._heap: list[tuple] = []

    def push(self, item: tuple) -> None:
        heapq.heappush(self._heap, item)

    def pop(self) -> tuple:
        return heapq.heappop(self._heap)

    @property
    def next_time(self) -> int:
        """Virtual time of the earliest queued event (queue must be non-empty)."""
        return self._heap[0][0]

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self._heap)

1	"""Bounded enumeration of message-fault combinations over a base scenario.
2	
3	``explore`` reuses the deterministic simulator for every combination: it
4	never reads the wall clock, never uses randomness and never creates files,
5	so identical PLAN input produces byte-identical output.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from itertools import combinations
11	
12	from .scenario import ScenarioError, _require_int, parse_scenario
13	from .simulate import _Simulator
14	
15	_PLAN_FIELDS = {
16	    "scenario",
17	    "candidates",
18	    "maxFaults",
19	    "maxCases",
20	    "minimizeFailures",
21	    "eventCandidates",
22	    "maxEventFaults",
23	}
24	_REQUIRED_PLAN_FIELDS = {"scenario", "candidates", "maxFaults", "maxCases"}
25	_EVENT_CANDIDATE_FIELDS = {"network", "node"}
26	
27	# Reports whose violation lists decide a case's status. A report the scenario
28	# does not enable is absent from the result and plays no part in the verdict.
29	_CHECKED_REPORTS = (
30	    "electionSafety",
31	    "logMatching",
32	    "stateMachineSafety",
33	    "linearizability",
34	    "liveness",
35	)
36	
37	
38	def _failure_signature(result: dict) -> tuple[str, ...]:
39	    """Names of the enabled reports whose violation list is non-empty, in
40	    fixed check-priority order. Two cases share a failure signature exactly
41	    when they violate the same set of invariants."""
42	    return tuple(
43	        key
44	        for key in _CHECKED_REPORTS
45	        if key in result and result[key]["violations"]
46	    )
47	
48	
49	def _merged_config(
50	    scenario_raw: dict,
51	    candidates: list,
52	    event_candidates: list,
53	    event_selected: tuple[int, ...],
54	) -> dict:
55	    """Validate and normalize the scenario for one event combination: the
56	    base scenario with every message-fault candidate presented as its
57	    messageFaults and the selected events appended to the corresponding
58	    collections. Base entries keep their positions, so at one timestamp
59	    same-kind base events are processed before the selected candidates (in
60	    candidate-index order), and network events still precede node events."""
61	    merged = dict(scenario_raw)
62	    merged["messageFaults"] = candidates
63	    network = [
64	        event_candidates[i]["network"] for i in event_selected if "network" in event_candidates[i]
65	    ]
66	    node = [event_candidates[i]["node"] for i in event_selected if "node" in event_candidates[i]]
67	    if network or "faults" in merged:
68	        merged["faults"] = list(merged.get("faults", [])) + network
69	    if node or "nodeEvents" in merged:
70	        merged["nodeEvents"] = list(merged.get("nodeEvents", [])) + node
71	    return parse_scenario(merged)
72	
73	
74	def run_explore(raw: object) -> dict:
75	    """Validate a decoded JSON PLAN and run every fault combination."""
76	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
77	        raise ScenarioError("plan must be a JSON object")
78	    unknown = sorted(set(raw) - _PLAN_FIELDS)
79	    if unknown:
80	        raise ScenarioError(f"unknown field(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")
81	    missing = sorted(_REQUIRED_PLAN_FIELDS - set(raw))
82	    if missing:
83	        raise ScenarioError(f"missing field(s): {', '.join(missing)}")
84	
85	    has_event_candidates = "eventCandidates" in raw
86	    has_max_event_faults = "maxEventFaults" in raw
87	    if has_event_candidates != has_max_event_faults:
88	        raise ScenarioError(
89	            "eventCandidates and maxEventFaults must be provided together"
90	        )
91	    events_enabled = has_event_candidates
92	
93	    minimize_failures = raw.get("minimizeFailures", False)
94	    if not isinstance(minimize_failures, bool):
95	        raise ScenarioError("minimizeFailures must be a boolean")
96	
97	    scenario_raw = raw["scenario"]
98	    if not isinstance(scenario_raw, dict):
99	        raise ScenarioError("scenario must be a JSON object")
100	    if "messageFaults" in scenario_raw:
101	        raise ScenarioError("scenario must not contain messageFaults")
102	
103	    candidates = raw["candidates"]
104	    if not isinstance(candidates, list):
105	        raise ScenarioError("candidates must be a list")
106	    if not candidates:
107	        raise ScenarioError("candidates must not be empty")
108	
109	    max_faults = _require_int(raw["maxFaults"], "maxFaults", 0)
110	    if max_faults > len(candidates):
111	        raise ScenarioError("maxFaults must not exceed the number of candidates")
112	    max_cases = _require_int(raw["maxCases"], "maxCases", 1)
113	
114	    event_candidates: list = []
115	    max_event_faults = 0
116	    if events_enabled:
117	        event_candidates = raw["eventCandidates"]
118	        if not isinstance(event_candidates, list):
119	            raise ScenarioError("eventCandidates must be a list")
120	        if not event_candidates:
121	            raise ScenarioError("eventCandidates must not be empty")
122	        for index, item in enumerate(event_candidates):
123	            label = f"eventCandidates[{index}]"
124	            if not isinstance(item, dict):
125	                raise ScenarioError(f"{label} must be an object")
126	            unknown = sorted(set(item) - _EVENT_CANDIDATE_FIELDS)
127	            if unknown:
128	                raise ScenarioError(
129	                    f"{label} has unknown field(s): {', '.join(unknown)}"
130	                )
131	            if len(set(item) & _EVENT_CANDIDATE_FIELDS) != 1:
132	                raise ScenarioError(
133	                    f"{label} must declare exactly one of network or node"
134	                )
135	        max_event_faults = _require_int(raw["maxEventFaults"], "maxEventFaults", 0)
136	        if max_event_faults > len(event_candidates):
137	            raise ScenarioError(
138	                "maxEventFaults must not exceed the number of event candidates"
139	            )
140	
141	    # Validate the base scenario and every candidate rule with the original
142	    # scenario validation by presenting the candidates as its messageFaults;
143	    # this also rejects duplicated full selectors. Each normalized rule keeps
144	    # its candidate index in its "index" field.
145	    combined = dict(scenario_raw)
146	    combined["messageFaults"] = candidates
147	    config = parse_scenario(combined)
148	    rules = config["messageFaults"]
149	
150	    # The empty combination comes first, then combinations of ascending size;
151	    # itertools.combinations yields index tuples in numeric lexicographic
152	    # order, and each tuple is ascending, so selected rules and events are
153	    # always injected in original candidate-index order.
154	    message_combos = [
155	        combo
156	        for size in range(max_faults + 1)
157	        for combo in combinations(range(len(candidates)), size)
158	    ]
159	    event_combos = [
160	        combo
161	        for size in range(max_event_faults + 1)
162	        for combo in combinations(range(len(event_candidates)), size)
163	    ]
164	
165	    total = len(message_combos) * len(event_combos)
166	    if total > max_cases:
167	        raise ScenarioError(
168	            f"combination count {total} exceeds maxCases {max_cases}"
169	        )
170	
171	    if events_enabled:
172	        # Every merged scenario is validated before any simulation runs:
173	        # first each event candidate on its own (in the base context, exactly
174	        # like the message-fault candidates above), then every enumerated
175	        # combination, whose appended events may jointly violate a constraint
176	        # such as crash/restart alternation.
177	        for index in range(len(event_candidates)):
178	            _merged_config(scenario_raw, candidates, event_candidates, (index,))
179	        event_configs = [
180	            _merged_config(scenario_raw, candidates, event_candidates, combo)
181	            for combo in event_combos
182	        ]
183	    else:
184	        event_configs = [config]
185	
186	    # Message-fault combinations form the outer loop in their established
187	    # order; within each, the empty event combination comes first, then
188	    # event combinations of ascending size in numeric lexicographic order.
189	    cases = []
190	    # Only populated while minimizing: signature -> list of
191	    # (selected index tuple, selected event index tuple, caseId).
192	    # Minimization never runs extra simulations; it only references cases
193	    # enumerated here, so those references do not count against maxCases.
194	    by_signature: dict[
195	        tuple[str, ...], list[tuple[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...], int]]
196	    ] = {}
197	    passed = 0
198	    case_id = 0
199	    for selected in message_combos:
200	        for event_index, event_selected in enumerate(event_combos):
201	            case_config = dict(event_configs[event_index])
202	            case_config["messageFaults"] = [rules[i] for i in selected]
203	            result = _Simulator(case_config).run()
204	            signature = _failure_signature(result)
205	            if signature:
206	                status = "failed"
207	            else:
208	                status = "passed"
209	                passed += 1
210	            case = {"caseId": case_id, "selected": list(selected)}
211	            if events_enabled:
212	                case["selectedEvents"] = list(event_selected)
213	            case["status"] = status
214	            case["result"] = result
215	            if minimize_failures and signature:
216	                by_signature.setdefault(signature, []).append(
217	                    (selected, event_selected, case_id)
218	                )
219	            cases.append(case)
220	            case_id += 1
221	
222	    if minimize_failures:
223	        for case in cases:
224	            if case["status"] != "failed":
225	                continue
226	            signature = _failure_signature(case["result"])
227	            selected = tuple(case["selected"])
228	            selected_events = tuple(case.get("selectedEvents", ()))
229	            # Every minimizing combination must be reachable by deleting
230	            # candidates of both kinds from this case (sub-combinations of
231	            # its selected indices) and reproduce its exact failure
232	            # signature: a combination that passes or that only shows other
233	            # violations is never selected. The fewest total candidates win;
234	            # ties are broken by the numeric lexicographic order of the
235	            # selected index array, then of the selectedEvents array. The
236	            # case itself always qualifies.
237	            minimal_selected, minimal_events, minimal_case_id = min(
238	                (
239	                    entry
240	                    for entry in by_signature[signature]
241	                    if set(entry[0]).issubset(selected)
242	                    and set(entry[1]).issubset(selected_events)
243	                ),
244	                key=lambda entry: (len(entry[0]) + len(entry[1]), entry[0], entry[1]),
245	            )
246	            case["failureReports"] = list(signature)
247	            case["minimalSelected"] = list(minimal_selected)
248	            if events_enabled:
249	                case["minimalSelectedEvents"] = list(minimal_events)
250	            case["minimalCaseId"] = minimal_case_id
251	
252	    return {
253	        "totalCases": len(cases),
254	        "passedCases": passed,
255	        "failedCases": len(cases) - passed,
256	        "cases": cases,
257	    }
258

1	"""Read-only replay verification of a saved ``simulate`` result.
2	
3	``replay`` reruns the deterministic simulation on the original scenario and
4	compares the freshly computed result against the saved result field by field.
5	It never reads the wall clock, never uses randomness and never creates or
6	modifies files, so identical input produces byte-identical output.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from .simulate import run_simulation
12	
13	
14	def _kind(value: object) -> str:
15	    """A JSON-level type tag. Booleans get their own tag so that ``true`` is
16	    never equal to the number 1, while ints and floats share ``number`` so
17	    that numbers compare by numeric value."""
18	    if value is None:
19	        return "null"
20	    if isinstance(value, bool):
21	        return "bool"
22	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
23	        return "number"
24	    if isinstance(value, str):
25	        return "string"
26	    if isinstance(value, list):
27	        return "array"
28	    return "object"
29	
30	
31	def _escape_token(token: str) -> str:
32	    """Escape one RFC 6901 reference token ('~' before '/')."""
33	    return token.replace("~", "~0").replace("/", "~1")
34	
35	
36	def _pointer(tokens: list[str]) -> str:
37	    if not tokens:
38	        return ""
39	    return "".join("/" + token for token in tokens)
40	
41	
42	def _first_difference(expected: object, actual: object, tokens: list[str]) -> str | None:
43	    """Return the RFC 6901 pointer of the first structural difference, or
44	    None when the two JSON values are equal.
45	
46	    Arrays are compared by ascending index; objects recurse over the union of
47	    both sides' keys in ascending Unicode code-point order. A type or scalar
48	    difference ends the comparison at the current position; when an array
49	    prefix matches but the lengths differ, the pointer names the first
50	    missing index.
51	    """
52	    expected_kind = _kind(expected)
53	    actual_kind = _kind(actual)
54	    if expected_kind != actual_kind:
55	        return _pointer(tokens)
56	
57	    if expected_kind in ("null", "bool", "number", "string"):
58	        if expected != actual:
59	            return _pointer(tokens)
60	        return None
61	
62	    if expected_kind == "array":
63	        shared = min(len(expected), len(actual))
64	        for index in range(shared):
65	            found = _first_difference(expected[index], actual[index], tokens + [str(index)])
66	            if found is not None:
67	                return found
68	        if len(expected) != len(actual):
69	            return _pointer(tokens + [str(shared)])
70	        return None
71	
72	    # Object: member order is irrelevant; visit the key union by Unicode code
73	    # point. A key present on only one side is itself the first difference.
74	    for key in sorted(set(expected) | set(actual)):
75	        token = _escape_token(key)
76	        if key not in expected or key not in actual:
77	            return _pointer(tokens + [token])
78	        found = _first_difference(expected[key], actual[key], tokens + [token])
79	        if found is not None:
80	            return found
81	    return None
82	
83	
84	def run_replay(scenario_raw: object, result_raw: object) -> dict:
85	    """Recompute the simulation for ``scenario_raw`` and compare it against
86	    the saved ``result_raw``.
87	
88	    Returns ``{"status": "matched"}`` on equality, otherwise an object with
89	    ``status: "mismatched"``, the RFC 6901 pointer of the first difference,
90	    presence flags for both sides and the present value(s). Scenario
91	    validation errors propagate as :class:`ScenarioError` exactly as in
92	    ``simulate``.
93	    """
94	    expected = run_simulation(scenario_raw)
95	
96	    path = _first_difference(expected, result_raw, [])
97	    if path is None:
98	        return {"status": "matched"}
99	
100	    mismatch = {
101	        "status": "mismatched",
102	        "path": path,
103	        "expectedPresent": False,
104	        "actualPresent": False,
105	    }
106	    expected_value, actual_value = _value_at(expected, path), _value_at(result_raw, path)
107	    if expected_value is not _MISSING:
108	        mismatch["expectedPresent"] = True
109	        mismatch["expected"] = expected_value
110	    if actual_value is not _MISSING:
111	        mismatch["actualPresent"] = True
112	        mismatch["actual"] = actual_value
113	    return mismatch
114	
115	
116	class _Missing:
117	    """Sentinel for a pointer position absent on one side (distinct from a
118	    real JSON null, which is a present value)."""
119	
120	
121	_MISSING = _Missing()
122	
123	
124	def _value_at(root: object, path: str) -> object:
125	    """Resolve an RFC 6901 pointer produced by the comparison against one
126	    side. Returns the ``_MISSING`` sentinel when an object member or array
127	    index is absent."""
128	    if path == "":
129	        return root
130	    current = root
131	    for raw_token in path.split("/")[1:]:
132	        token = raw_token.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~")
133	        if isinstance(current, dict):
134	            if token in current:
135	                current = current[token]
136	            else:
137	                return _MISSING
138	        elif isinstance(current, list) and token.isascii() and token.isdigit():
139	            index = int(token)
140	            if 0 <= index < len(current):
141	                current = current[index]
142	            else:
143	                return _MISSING
144	        else:
145	            return _MISSING
146	    return current

3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import argparse
6	import json
7	import math
8	import sys
9	
10	from . import __version__
11	from .explore import run_explore
12	from .replay import run_replay
13	from .scenario import ScenarioError
14	from .simulate import run_simulation
15	
16	
17	def _reject_json_constant(value: str) -> None:
18	    raise ValueError(f"non-finite JSON number token: {value}")
19	
20	
21	def _reject_non_finite(value: object) -> None:
22	    """Reject every non-finite number anywhere in a decoded JSON tree.
23	
24	    ``parse_constant`` refuses the bare NaN/Infinity/-Infinity literals, but a
25	    number whose exponent overflows float range (e.g. 1e1000) decodes to a
26	    non-finite float without ever being seen as a constant token; such values
27	    can hide at any depth (for example inside a client command), so the whole
28	    tree is checked after decoding. Object keys and the strings "NaN" /
29	    "Infinity" / "-Infinity" are ordinary strings and never rejected.
30	    """
31	    stack = [value]
32	    while stack:
33	        current = stack.pop()
34	        if isinstance(current, float):
35	            if not math.isfinite(current):
36	                raise ValueError(f"non-finite JSON number: {current!r}")
37	        elif isinstance(current, dict):
38	            stack.extend(current.values())
39	        elif isinstance(current, list):
40	            stack.extend(current)
41	
42	
43	def _load_strict_json(text: str) -> object:
44	    """Decode strict JSON: no NaN/Infinity/-Infinity tokens and no non-finite
45	    numbers anywhere in the tree."""
46	    raw = json.loads(text, parse_constant=_reject_json_constant)
47	    _reject_non_finite(raw)
48	    return raw
49	
50	
51	def _cmd_simulate(path: str) -> int:
52	    try:
53	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
54	            text = handle.read()
55	    except OSError as exc:
56	        print(f"error: cannot read scenario file: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
57	        return 2
58	    except UnicodeDecodeError:
59	        print(f"error: scenario file is not valid UTF-8: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
60	        return 2
61	    try:
62	        raw = _load_strict_json(text)
63	    except ValueError as exc:
64	        print(f"error: invalid JSON: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
65	        return 2
66	    try:
67	        result = run_simulation(raw)
68	    except ScenarioError as exc:
69	        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
70	        return 2
71	    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
72	    return 0
73	
74	
75	def _cmd_explore(path: str) -> int:
76	    try:
77	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
78	            text = handle.read()
79	    except OSError as exc:
80	        print(f"error: cannot read plan file: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
81	        return 2
82	    except UnicodeDecodeError:
83	        print(f"error: plan file is not valid UTF-8: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
84	        return 2
85	    try:
86	        raw = _load_strict_json(text)
87	    except ValueError as exc:
88	        print(f"error: invalid JSON: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
89	        return 2
90	    try:
91	        result = run_explore(raw)
92	    except ScenarioError as exc:
93	        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
94	        return 2
95	    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
96	    return 0
97	
98	
99	def _read_utf8_json(path: str, kind: str) -> tuple[bool, object]:
100	    """Read and decode a UTF-8 JSON file for replay. Returns (ok, value);
101	    on failure prints one ``error:`` line to stderr and returns (False,
102	    None). ``kind`` labels the file in the messages."""
103	    try:
104	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
105	            text = handle.read()
106	    except OSError as exc:
107	        print(f"error: cannot read {kind} file: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
108	        return False, None
109	    except UnicodeDecodeError:
110	        print(f"error: {kind} file is not valid UTF-8: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
111	        return False, None
112	    try:
113	        # Strict JSON boundary: refuse the non-standard NaN/Infinity tokens
114	        # and any non-finite number an exponent overflow could decode to,
115	        # anywhere in the tree.
116	        return True, _load_strict_json(text)
117	    except ValueError as exc:
118	        print(f"error: invalid JSON in {kind} file: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
119	        return False, None
120	
121	
122	def _cmd_replay(scenario_path: str, result_path: str) -> int:
123	    ok, scenario_raw = _read_utf8_json(scenario_path, "scenario")
124	    if not ok:
125	        return 2
126	    ok, result_raw = _read_utf8_json(result_path, "result")
127	    if not ok:
128	        return 2
129	    # A non-object RESULT cannot carry the comparison contract (status is
130	    # reported as mismatched only when the top level is an object).
131	    if not isinstance(result_raw, dict):
132	        print("error: result file must contain a JSON object", file=sys.stderr)
133	        return 2
134	    try:
135	        report = run_replay(scenario_raw, result_raw)
136	    except ScenarioError as exc:
137	        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
138	        return 2
139	    # Compact, member order fixed by construction: byte-identical for
140	    # identical input.
141	    print(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")))
142	    return 0 if report["status"] == "matched" else 1
143	
144	
145	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
146	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="consensus-protocol-lab", description="Deterministic simulation lab for Raft-style consensus protocols")
147	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")
148	    sub.add_parser("version", help="print the current version")
149	    simulate = sub.add_parser("simulate", help="run a deterministic Raft leader-election simulation")
150	    simulate.add_argument("scenario", help="path to a UTF-8 JSON scenario file")
151	    explore = sub.add_parser("explore", help="enumerate bounded message-fault combinations over a base scenario")
152	    explore.add_argument("plan", help="path to a UTF-8 JSON plan file")
153	    replay = sub.add_parser("replay", help="recompute a simulation and field-compare it against a saved result")
154	    replay.add_argument("scenario", help="path to the UTF-8 JSON scenario file")
155	    replay.add_argument("result", help="path to a UTF-8 JSON file holding a simulate result")
156	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
157	
158	    if args.command == "version":
159	        print(__version__)
160	        return 0
161	    if args.command == "simulate":
162	        return _cmd_simulate(args.scenario)
163	    if args.command == "explore":
164	        return _cmd_explore(args.plan)
165	    if args.command == "replay":
166	        return _cmd_replay(args.scenario, args.result)
167	
168	    parser.print_help()
169	    return 0
170	
171	
172	if __name__ == "__main__":
173	    sys.exit(main())

2	
3	Everything here is read-only over the finished simulation: the timeline, the
4	final node states and the bookkeeping accumulated during the run are
5	projected into the client/membership/read summaries and the election-safety,
6	log-matching, state-machine-safety, linearizability and liveness reports.
7	Nothing in this module mutates simulator state.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import json
13	
14	from .node import CONFIG_JOINT, KIND_CONFIG, _Node
15	
16	
17	def _log_matching_violations(sim) -> list[dict]:
18	    """Same index and term, but different content (id/command for client
19	    commands, or the configuration payload) across nodes, including
20	    indices folded into snapshots or occupied by configuration entries."""
21	    violations = []
22	    max_len = max((st.last_log_index() for st in sim.state.values()), default=0)
23	    for index in range(1, max_len + 1):
24	        by_term: dict[int, dict[tuple, dict]] = {}
25	        for name in sim.node_names:
26	            st = sim.state[name]
27	            entry = sim._entry_view(st, index)
28	            if entry is None:
29	                continue
30	            if entry.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG:
31	                marker = json.dumps(
32	                    [
33	                        entry["id"],
34	                        KIND_CONFIG,
35	                        entry["entryType"],
36	                        entry.get("config"),
37	                        entry.get("action"),
38	                        entry.get("member"),
39	                    ],
40	                    ensure_ascii=False,
41	                    sort_keys=True,
42	                )
43	                bucket_view = {
44	                    "id": entry["id"],
45	                    "kind": KIND_CONFIG,
46	                    "entryType": entry["entryType"],
47	                    "config": entry.get("config"),
48	                    "nodes": [],
49	                }
50	            else:
51	                marker = json.dumps([entry["id"], entry["command"]], ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)
52	                bucket_view = {"id": entry["id"], "command": entry["command"], "nodes": []}
53	            bucket = by_term.setdefault(entry["term"], {}).setdefault(marker, bucket_view)
54	            bucket["nodes"].append(name)
55	        for term, variants in sorted(by_term.items()):
56	            if len(variants) > 1:
57	                violations.append(
58	                    {
59	                        "index": index,
60	                        "term": term,
61	                        "variants": [bucket for _marker, bucket in sorted(variants.items())],
62	                    }
63	                )
64	    return violations

66	def _state_machine_safety_violations(sim) -> list[dict]:
67	    """Different nodes applied different entries at the same index.
68	    Configuration entries participate in index alignment alongside client
69	    commands, and applied histories recovered from snapshots are covered."""
70	    violations = []
71	    max_applied = max((st.last_applied for st in sim.state.values()), default=0)
72	    for index in range(1, max_applied + 1):
73	        variants: dict[str, dict] = {}
74	        for name in sim.node_names:
75	            st = sim.state[name]
76	            if index > st.last_applied:
77	                continue
78	            entry = st.applied[index - 1]
79	            if entry.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG:
80	                marker = json.dumps(
81	                    [
82	                        entry["term"],
83	                        entry["id"],
84	                        KIND_CONFIG,
85	                        entry["entryType"],
86	                        entry.get("config"),
87	                    ],
88	                    ensure_ascii=False,
89	                    sort_keys=True,
90	                )
91	                bucket = variants.setdefault(
92	                    marker,
93	                    {
94	                        "term": entry["term"],
95	                        "id": entry["id"],
96	                        "kind": KIND_CONFIG,
97	                        "entryType": entry["entryType"],
98	                        "config": entry.get("config"),
99	                        "nodes": [],
100	                    },
101	                )
102	            else:
103	                marker = json.dumps([entry["term"], entry["id"], entry["command"]], ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)
104	                bucket = variants.setdefault(
105	                    marker, {"term": entry["term"], "id": entry["id"], "command": entry["command"], "nodes": []}
106	                )
107	            bucket["nodes"].append(name)
108	        if len(variants) > 1:
109	            violations.append(
110	                {"index": index, "variants": [bucket for marker, bucket in sorted(variants.items())]}
111	            )
112	    return violations
113	
114	def _clients_report(sim) -> dict:
115	    grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {
116	        "committed": [],
117	        "superseded": [],
118	        "pending": [],
119	        "rejected": [],
120	    }
121	
122	    def find_applied(command_id: str) -> dict | None:
123	        for name in sim.node_names:
124	            for entry in sim.state[name].applied:
125	                if entry["id"] == command_id:
126	                    return entry
127	        return None
128	
129	    def in_any_log(command_id: str) -> dict | None:
130	        for name in sim.node_names:
131	            for entry in sim.state[name].log:
132	                if entry["id"] == command_id:
133	                    return entry
134	        return None
135	
136	    for command in sim.commands:
137	        command_id = command["id"]
138	        if command_id in sim.rejected:
139	            rejected = sim.rejected[command_id]
140	            grouped["rejected"].append(
141	                {
142	                    "id": command_id,
143	                    "node": command["node"],
144	                    "reason": rejected["reason"],
145	                    "knownLeader": rejected["knownLeader"],
146	                }
147	            )
148	            continue
149	        applied = find_applied(command_id)
150	        if applied is not None:
151	            grouped["committed"].append(
152	                {
153	                    "id": command_id,
154	                    "node": command["node"],
155	                    "index": applied["index"],
156	                    "term": applied["term"],
157	                }
158	            )
159	            continue
160	        present = in_any_log(command_id)
161	        if present is not None:
162	            grouped["pending"].append(
163	                {
164	                    "id": command_id,
165	                    "node": command["node"],
166	                    "index": present["index"],
167	                    "term": present["term"],
168	                }
169	            )
170	        else:
171	            grouped["superseded"].append({"id": command_id, "node": command["node"]})
172	    return grouped
173	
174	def _node_report(sim, name: str, st: _Node) -> dict:
175	    report = {
176	        "role": st.role,
177	        "term": st.term,
178	        "votedFor": st.voted_for,
179	        "knownLeader": st.known_leader,
180	        "log": [dict(entry) for entry in st.log],
181	        "commitIndex": st.commit_index,
182	        "lastApplied": st.last_applied,
183	        "applied": [dict(entry) for entry in st.applied],
184	    }
185	    if sim.membership_enabled:
186	        # Voter/learner according to the node's newest configuration,
187	        # which governs voting and campaigning even before it commits.
188	        report["membershipRole"] = (
189	            "voter" if sim._is_voter(name, st.latest_config(sim.initial_config)) else "learner"
190	        )
191	    if sim.snapshot_threshold is not None:
192	        if st.snapshot_index > 0:
193	            report["snapshot"] = {
194	                "lastIncludedIndex": st.snapshot_index,
195	                "lastIncludedTerm": st.snapshot_term,
196	            }
197	        else:
198	            report["snapshot"] = None
199	    if sim.node_events_provided:
200	        report["online"] = st.online
201	        report["restartCount"] = st.restart_count
202	    return report
203	
204	def _membership_report(sim) -> dict:
205	    # The reference node deterministically has the greatest committed
206	    # position, then the greatest log length (declared node order breaks
207	    # ties): committed truth dominates, so a deposed leader's stale
208	    # uncommitted suffix cannot describe a phase the cluster left.
209	    ref_name = max(
210	        sim.node_names,
211	        key=lambda name: (
212	            sim.state[name].commit_index,
213	            sim.state[name].last_log_index(),
214	            -sim.index[name],
215	        ),
216	    )
217	    ref = sim.state[ref_name]
218	    committed = ref.committed_config(sim.initial_config)
219	    latest = ref.latest_config(sim.initial_config)
220	
221	    if latest.get("type") == CONFIG_JOINT:
222	        old, new = sim._config_groups(latest)
223	        current_stable = sorted(old)
224	        joint = {"id": _latest_joint_id(ref),
225	                 "old": sorted(old), "new": sorted(new)}
226	    elif committed.get("type") == CONFIG_JOINT:
227	        old, new = sim._config_groups(committed)
228	        current_stable = sorted(old)
229	        joint = {"id": _latest_joint_id(ref),
230	                 "old": sorted(old), "new": sorted(new)}
231	    else:
232	        _, stable_voters = sim._config_groups(committed)
233	        current_stable = sorted(stable_voters)
234	        joint = None
235	
236	    joint_ids = set()
237	    for st in sim.state.values():
238	        for applied in st.applied:
239	            if applied.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG and applied["entryType"] == CONFIG_JOINT:
240	                joint_ids.add(applied["id"])
241	        for log_entry in st.log:
242	            if log_entry.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG and log_entry["entryType"] == CONFIG_JOINT:
243	                joint_ids.add(log_entry["id"])
244	
245	    changes = []
246	    for change in sim.changes:
247	        change_id = change["id"]
248	        result = sim.change_results.get(change_id)
249	        entry = {
250	            "id": change_id,
251	            "node": change["node"],
252	            "action": change["action"],
253	            "member": change["member"],
254	        }
255	        if result is None or result.get("outcome") == "pending":
256	            entry["outcome"] = "pending"
257	            if sim.pending_catchup is not None and sim.pending_catchup["id"] == change_id:
258	                entry["phase"] = "catchingUp"
259	            elif change_id in joint_ids:
260	                phase_info = result.get("jointPhase") if result else None
261	                entry["phase"] = "joint"
262	                if phase_info is not None:
263	                    entry["joint"] = {
264	                        "old": sorted(phase_info["old"]),
265	                        "new": sorted(phase_info["new"]),
266	                    }
267	            else:
268	                entry["phase"] = "catchingUp"
269	        elif result.get("outcome") == "rejected":
270	            entry["outcome"] = "rejected"
271	            entry["reason"] = result["reason"]
272	        else:
273	            entry["outcome"] = "committed"
274	            entry["index"] = result["index"]
275	            entry["term"] = result["term"]
276	        changes.append(entry)
277	
278	    return {
279	        "initial": sorted(sim.initial_config["new"]),
280	        "current": current_stable,
281	        "joint": joint,
282	        "changes": changes,
283	    }
284	
285	def _latest_config_entry_id(st: _Node, entry_type: str) -> str | None:
286	    """The id of the newest committed configuration entry of a type,
287	    looking through the snapshot into the applied history."""
288	    found = None
289	    for entry in st.applied:
290	        if entry.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG and entry["entryType"] == entry_type:
291	            found = entry["id"]
292	    upper = min(st.commit_index, st.last_log_index())
293	    for i in range(st.snapshot_index + 1, upper + 1):
294	        entry = st.log[i - 1 - st.snapshot_index]
295	        if entry.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG and entry["entryType"] == entry_type:
296	            found = entry["id"]
297	    return found
298	
299	def _latest_joint_id(st: _Node) -> str | None:
300	    """The id of the newest joint configuration entry the reference node
301	    holds, including one appended but not yet committed."""
302	    found = _latest_config_entry_id(st, CONFIG_JOINT)
303	    for entry in st.log:
304	        if entry.get("kind") == KIND_CONFIG and entry["entryType"] == CONFIG_JOINT:
305	            found = entry["id"]
306	    return found
307	
308	def _reads_report(sim) -> list[dict]:
309	    """The final outcome of every read query, in input order. Queries
310	    still awaiting a majority confirmation when the simulation ends are
311	    reported as pending."""
312	    reads = []
313	    for query in sim.read_queries:
314	        query_id = query["id"]
315	        result = sim.read_results.get(query_id)
316	        if result is None:
317	            pending = sim.pending_reads[query_id]
318	            result = {
319	                "outcome": "pending",
320	                "term": pending["term"],
321	                "readIndex": pending["readIndex"],
322	            }
323	        reads.append({"id": query_id, "node": query["node"], **result})
324	    return reads
325	
326	def _linearizability_violations(sim) -> list[dict]:
327	    """Per completed read, checked in input order:
328	    - nonPrefix: the returned state is not the complete client-command
329	      prefix of the serving leader's applied history up to readIndex
330	      (configuration entries excluded, compacted commands included);
331	    - staleRead: the state omits a write that was already committed when
332	      the query was accepted."""
333	    violations = []
334	    for query in sim.read_queries:
335	        query_id = query["id"]
336	        result = sim.read_results.get(query_id)
337	        if result is None or result.get("outcome") != "completed":
338	            continue
339	        read_index = result["readIndex"]
340	        st = sim.state[query["node"]]
341	        expected = [
342	            sim._read_state_entry(entry)
343	            for entry in st.applied[:read_index]
344	            if entry.get("kind") != KIND_CONFIG
345	        ]
346	        if result["state"] != expected:
347	            violations.append(
348	                {"type": "nonPrefix", "id": query_id, "readIndex": read_index}
349	            )
350	        present = {entry["id"] for entry in result["state"]}
351	        missing = sorted(sim.read_required.get(query_id, set()) - present)
352	        if missing:
353	            violations.append(
354	                {"type": "staleRead", "id": query_id, "missing": missing}
355	            )
356	    return violations
357	
358	def _liveness_report(sim) -> dict:
359	    """Per-check outcomes in input order; every failed outcome is also
360	    listed as a violation."""
361	    checks = [sim.liveness_results[check["id"]] for check in sim.liveness_checks]
362	    violations = [check for check in checks if check["status"] == "failed"]
363	    return {"checks": checks, "violations": violations}
364	
365	def build_report(sim) -> dict:
366	    leaders = {str(term): names for term, names in sorted(sim.leaders_by_term.items())}
367	    violations = [
368	        {"term": term, "leaders": list(names)}
369	        for term, names in sorted(sim.leaders_by_term.items())
370	        if len(names) > 1
371	    ]
372	    report = {
373	        "timeline": sim.timeline,
374	        "nodes": {
375	            name: _node_report(sim, name, st)
376	            for name, st in sim.state.items()
377	        },
378	        "clients": _clients_report(sim),
379	    }
380	    if sim.read_queries_provided:

5	structural and cross-reference checks run here, before any event is
6	scheduled, so the simulation core only ever sees a legal scenario.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	_TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS = {

34	    "membershipChanges",

39	}

41	_MESSAGE_FAULT_FIELDS = {"from", "to", "message", "occurrence", "action", "delay"}
42	_MESSAGE_FAULT_REQUIRED = {"from", "to", "message", "occurrence", "action"}
43	_MESSAGE_KINDS = (
44	    "requestVote",
45	    "voteReply",
46	    "preVote",

56	# Pre-vote traffic exists only while the optional phase is enabled; a rule
57	# referencing either kind in a preVote-less scenario makes the scenario illegal.
58	_PRE_VOTE_MESSAGE_KINDS = ("preVote", "preVoteReply")
59	_CLIENT_COMMAND_FIELDS = {"time", "node", "id", "command"}
60	_NODE_EVENT_FIELDS = {"time", "node", "action"}
61	_MEMBERSHIP_CHANGE_FIELDS = {"time", "node", "id", "action", "member"}

76	class ScenarioError(Exception):
77	    """The scenario input is invalid."""
78	
79	
80	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
81	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
82	
83	
84	def _require_int(value: object, name: str, minimum: int) -> int:
85	    if not _is_int(value):
86	        raise ScenarioError(f"{name} must be an integer")
87	    if value < minimum:
88	        if minimum > 0:
89	            raise ScenarioError(f"{name} must be a positive integer")
90	        raise ScenarioError(f"{name} must be a non-negative integer")
91	    return value
92	
93	
94	def parse_scenario(raw: object) -> dict:
95	    """Validate the decoded JSON scenario and return a normalized config."""
96	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
97	        raise ScenarioError("scenario must be a JSON object")
98	    unknown = sorted(set(raw) - _TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS)
99	    if unknown:
100	        raise ScenarioError(f"unknown field(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")
101	    missing = sorted(_REQUIRED_FIELDS - set(raw))
102	    if missing:
103	        raise ScenarioError(f"missing field(s): {', '.join(missing)}")
104	
105	    nodes = raw["nodes"]
106	    if not isinstance(nodes, list) or len(nodes) < 3:
107	        raise ScenarioError("nodes must be a list of at least three names")
108	    for name in nodes:
109	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
110	            raise ScenarioError("node names must be non-empty strings")
111	    if len(set(nodes)) != len(nodes):
112	        raise ScenarioError("node names must be unique")
113	
114	    duration = _require_int(raw["duration"], "duration", 0)
115	    heartbeat = _require_int(raw["heartbeatInterval"], "heartbeatInterval", 1)
116	    delay = _require_int(raw["messageDelay"], "messageDelay", 0)
117	
118	    timeouts_raw = raw["electionTimeouts"]
119	    if _is_int(timeouts_raw):
120	        _require_int(timeouts_raw, "electionTimeouts", 1)
121	        timeouts = {name: timeouts_raw for name in nodes}
122	    elif isinstance(timeouts_raw, dict):
123	        unknown_nodes = sorted(set(timeouts_raw) - set(nodes))
124	        if unknown_nodes:
125	            raise ScenarioError(
126	                f"electionTimeouts references unknown node(s): {', '.join(unknown_nodes)}"
127	            )
128	        missing_nodes = sorted(set(nodes) - set(timeouts_raw))
129	        if missing_nodes:

132	            )

136	    else:

138	
139	    # The optional pre-vote phase is opt-in: omitted or false keeps every
140	    # legacy scenario's behavior (and output) byte for byte, and the

"""Tests for the optional pre-vote phase."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import pytest

from consensus_lab.cli import main
from consensus_lab.simulate import (
    ROLE_FOLLOWER,
    ROLE_LEADER,
    ROLE_PRECANDIDATE,
    _Simulator,
    parse_scenario,
)


def _write(path_dir, name, value):
    path = path_dir / name
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value), encoding="utf-8")
    return str(path)


def _base_scenario(**overrides):
    scenario = {
        "nodes": ["a", "b", "c"],
        "duration": 500,
        "electionTimeouts": {"a": 100, "b": 150, "c": 200},
        "heartbeatInterval": 50,
        "messageDelay": 10,
    }
    scenario.update(overrides)
    return scenario


def _run(tmp_path, capsys, scenario):
    path = _write(tmp_path, "scenario.json", scenario)
    code = main(["simulate", path])
    out, err = capsys.readouterr()
    return code, out, err


def _run_ok(tmp_path, capsys, scenario):
    code, out, err = _run(tmp_path, capsys, scenario)
    assert code == 0 and err == ""
    return json.loads(out)


def _by_type(result, event_type):
    return [e for e in result["timeline"] if e["type"] == event_type]


# -- backward compatibility -------------------------------------------------


def test_pre_vote_omitted_false_and_legacy_are_byte_identical(tmp_path, capsys):
    plain = _base_scenario()
    _, out_plain, _ = _run(tmp_path, capsys, plain)

    _, out_false, _ = _run(tmp_path, capsys, _base_scenario(preVote=False))
    assert out_false == out_plain

    # A richer legacy scenario (every feature on) is unchanged too.
    rich = _base_scenario(
        duration=900,
        snapshotThreshold=3,
        initialMembers=["a", "b", "c"],
        faults=[{"time": 120, "action": "partition", "groups": [["a"], ["b", "c"]]},
                {"time": 300, "action": "heal"}],
        clientCommands=[{"time": 200, "node": "a", "id": "x1", "command": 1}],
        nodeEvents=[{"time": 400, "node": "c", "action": "crash"},
                    {"time": 600, "node": "c", "action": "restart"}],
        membershipChanges=[{"time": 250, "node": "a", "id": "m1",
                            "action": "remove", "member": "c"}],
        readQueries=[{"time": 350, "node": "a", "id": "r1"}],
        livenessChecks=[{"id": "l1", "type": "leaderElected",
                         "startTime": 0, "deadline": 500}],
        messageFaults=[{"from": "a", "to": "b", "message": "heartbeat",
                        "occurrence": 9, "action": "drop"}],
    )
    _, out_rich_legacy, _ = _run(tmp_path, capsys, rich)
    rich_false = dict(rich)
    rich_false["preVote"] = False
    _, out_rich_false, _ = _run(tmp_path, capsys, rich_false)
    assert out_rich_false == out_rich_legacy


def test_pre_vote_disabled_emits_no_pre_vote_traffic(tmp_path, capsys):
    result = _run_ok(tmp_path, capsys, _base_scenario())
    messages = {e.get("message") for e in result["timeline"]}
    assert "preVote" not in messages
    assert "preVoteReply" not in messages
    assert all(n["role"] != ROLE_PRECANDIDATE for n in result["nodes"].values())


# -- happy path --------------------------------------------------------------


def test_pre_vote_precedes_the_real_election_without_bumping_term(tmp_path, capsys):
